title_en: Li Deyong v. Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd., Chongqing Yunyang Sub-branch — dispute over a savings deposit contract
ruling_gist_en: Article 13 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: 'The parties to a contract shall conclude the contract by means of offer and acceptance.' Article 25 provides: 'The contract is concluded when the acceptance becomes effective.' Pursuant to the above legal provisions, a depositor who claims to have established a savings deposit contract with a bank shall prove that the depositor and the bank have respectively made an offer and an acceptance, which meets the requirements for contract formation. Where a depositor claims to have established a savings contract with a bank on the basis of a forged certificate of deposit by a criminal, the people's court shall determine whether the depositor and the bank have respectively made an offer and an acceptance with regard to the savings matters. Where it cannot be found that the parties have established a savings contract, an action brought by the depositor on the basis of a forged certificate of deposit shall be handled as a general certificate of deposit dispute in accordance with the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Certificate of Deposit Disputes.

full_text_en:
Li Deyong v. China Agricultural Bank Co., Ltd. Chongqing Yunyang Branch — dispute over savings deposit contract

【Ruling Summary】

Article 13 of the Contract Law of the PRC provides: "The parties conclude a contract by making an offer and accepting the offer." Article 25 provides: "A contract is established when the acceptance becomes effective." In accordance with the above legal provisions, a depositor who claims to have formed a savings deposit contract with a bank shall prove that the depositor and the bank have respectively made an offer and an acceptance, meeting the requirements for the formation of a contract. Where a depositor claims to have formed a savings deposit contract with a bank based on a deposit certificate forged by a criminal, the people's court shall determine whether the depositor and the bank have respectively made an offer and an acceptance with respect to the deposit matter. If it cannot be determined that a savings deposit contract has been formed between the two parties, the lawsuit filed by the depositor based on the forged deposit certificate shall be dealt with as a general deposit certificate dispute in accordance with the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Trial of Deposit Certificate Dispute Cases.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2013) Min Ti Zi No. 95

Re-Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Li Deyong, male, Han ethnicity, born on November 14, 1973, residing in Banan District, Chongqing.

Agent ad litem: Liang Chunrong, lawyer at Chongqing Kangfa Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): China Agricultural Bank Co., Ltd. Chongqing Yunyang Branch, domiciled at No. 1178 Yunyang Avenue, Shuangjiang Town, Yunyang County, Chongqing.

Person in charge: Yan Zhiming, person in charge of this branch.

Agents ad litem: He Mu, male, Han ethnicity, born on March 6, 1985, employee of Chongqing Municipal Branch of China Agricultural Bank Co., Ltd., residing in Yuzhong District, Chongqing.

Agent ad litem: Shang Wanting, lawyer at Beijing Tianrui Law Firm.

The re-applicant, Li Deyong, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2012) Yu Gao Fa Min Zhong Zi No. 00014 rendered by the Chongqing High People's Court in the case of dispute over savings deposit contract with the respondent, China Agricultural Bank Co., Ltd. Chongqing Yunyang Branch (hereinafter referred to as Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch), applied to this Court for retrial. This Court, by civil ruling (2012) Min Shen Zi No. 1486 dated May 2, 2013, decided to bring the case for retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel according to law and held a hearing on July 2, 2013. Liang Chunrong, agent ad litem of Li Deyong, and He Mu and Shang Wanting, agents ad litem of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

The Chongqing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court found at first instance: Tan Wenli was an employee of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch. In January 2009, he was transferred from the Yunjiang Avenue Office of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch to the Zhaiba Office to serve as a client manager. Tang Housheng was the legal representative of Shengzhou Water Conservancy Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shengzhou Company), which publicly claimed to be the owner entity of the Meifeng Reservoir Project in Yunyang County, Chongqing, and engaged in "capital attraction" in that capacity. Tang Housheng, through Zeng Yong, became acquainted with Liu Hong, the legal representative of Chongqing Chuangtou Asset Management Co., Ltd. On December 17, 2008, Tang Housheng and Liu Hong signed a "Letter of Commitment," agreeing that if the capital attraction succeeded, they would pay Liu Hong 8% interest. Tang Housheng, Liu Hong, and Liu Daiyi conspired to defraud funds by using counterfeit deposit certificates under the pretext of attracting deposits with high interest rates and engaging in "off-balance-sheet" operations. Liu Hong sent copies of Shengzhou Company's materials to Zhong Daoming, promising Zhong Daoming a monthly interest rate of 7%, and instructed Zhong Daoming to contact depositors, with the interest rate to be offered to the depositors left to Zhong Daoming's discretion. On January 14, 2009, Zhong Daoming, as the depositor, and Liu Daiyi, as the representative of Shengzhou Company, signed a "Capital Attraction and Deposit Agreement." Zhong Daoming, through Shao Anmi, contacted Li Deyong, telling Li Deyong that depositing money at Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch would yield a high interest return. Zhong Daoming collected a deposit of RMB 30,000 from the borrowing enterprise's representative, Liu Daiyi, and informed Li Deyong, agreeing to offer Li Deyong a monthly interest rate of 5.5%. Li Deyong arrived in Yunyang County, Chongqing, on January 14, 2009, and processed the deposit on January 15, 2009.

On December 27, 2008, Tang Housheng instructed Liu Daiyi to use Xiong Tongpei's identity card to deposit RMB 300 at the Xingjiawan Office of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch, obtaining a three-month fixed deposit certificate for that amount. The teller handling the transaction was Cheng Jian. Tan Wenli, using his position at Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch and his acquaintance with Cheng Jian, learned that Cheng Jian would be working on January 15, 2009. Liu Hong, Liu Daiyi, and others, based on the sample of the above-mentioned RMB 300 fixed deposit certificate, counterfeited a China Agricultural Bank deposit certificate, which stated: "Account holder: Li Deyong, amount: ten million yuan, deposit date: 2009/01/15, term: three months, annual interest rate: 1.71%, issuing bank: Yunyang Branch Xingjiawan Business Office, teller: Cheng Jian, stamped with the business seal of China Agricultural Bank Chongqing Xingjiawan Branch." Tang Housheng, in Tan Wenli's office, took advantage of Tan Wenli's inattention and removed a document stamped with the seal of "China Agricultural Bank Yunyang County Branch," and used the impression of its seal to arrange for the engraving of a counterfeit seal of "China Agricultural Bank Yunyang County Branch."

On the morning of January 15, 2009, Liu Hong, Liu Daiyi, and others led Li Deyong to the office of Tan Wenli at the former Yunjiang Avenue Office of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch, and introduced Tan Wenli to Li Deyong as "President Tan." Tan Wenli handed Li Deyong a pre-prepared "Letter of Commitment," which stated: "Our bank's client, Li Deyong, has deposited a three-month fixed deposit of RMB 10 million in our bank. Our bank hereby makes the following commitment: This deposit shall not be mortgaged, inquired into, or prematurely withdrawn within three months, and we guarantee that upon maturity, our bank shall, based on Li Deyong's deposit certificate and the original of this letter of commitment, redeem the full amount of this RMB 10 million deposit. We hereby commit. China Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch, January 15, 2009." After Li Deyong read it, Tan Wenli signed the "Letter of Commitment." Liu Daiyi stated that the bank's official seal would be delivered immediately, and instructed someone to bring the privately engraved "China Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch" seal and stamp it on the "Letter of Commitment." After the "Letter of Commitment" was signed and stamped, Tan Wenli, Liu Daiyi, and Tang Houpei first went to the Xingjiawan Office of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch. They placed the pre-counterfeited China Agricultural Bank deposit certificate into an envelope, and Tan Wenli handed the envelope to the bank teller, Cheng Jian, telling Cheng Jian that he would be transferring a sum of money shortly and asked him to hand the envelope back to Tan Wenli after completing the transaction. Cheng Jian took the envelope and placed it on his desk. Subsequently, Liu Hong and Zeng Yong brought Li Deyong to the service window at the Xingjiawan Office of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch where Tan Wenli was standing in front of teller Cheng Jian. Li Deyong handed his bank card (number 6228 ××××××××××××1610) and identity card to Cheng Jian. Tan Wenli also handed Cheng Jian a bank card he had previously opened using Ren Qiming's identity card, and told Cheng Jian to transfer RMB 10 million from Li Deyong's bank card to the bank card Tan Wenli had handed over. After Li Deyong entered his password, Cheng Jian transferred RMB 10 million from his bank card, which entered the internal accounts of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch (31——1002××××××××0003 and 31——4703××××××××0045), and then transferred the funds to the bank card account of Ren Qiming (6228 ×××××××××××0016) provided by Tan Wenli. Cheng Jian had Li Deyong sign the bank card withdrawal slip and had Tan Wenli sign the deposit slip for the bank card in the name of Ren Qiming. Cheng Jian then returned the RMB 10 million withdrawal transaction receipt, along with Li Deyong's bank card and identity card, to Li Deyong, and handed the RMB 10 million deposit receipt for the bank card in the name of Ren Qiming, the bank card, and the envelope that Tan Wenli had previously given to Cheng Jian for safekeeping, to Tan Wenli. Tan Wenli, upon receiving the envelope, handed it to Li Deyong. Li Deyong and Tan Wenli returned together to the Yunjiang Avenue Office of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch, where Tan Wenli gave Li Deyong the previously signed and stamped "Letter of Commitment." Subsequently, Tan Wenli, Liu Hong, Li Deyong, and others went together to the Zhaiba Office of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch. According to the agreed interest rate, they transferred an interest difference of RMB 2.4 million from the bank card in the name of Ren Qiming to Liu Hong's bank card, and Liu Hong transferred RMB 1.65 million (based on the previously agreed monthly interest of 5.5%) from his bank card to Li Deyong's bank card. After Tang Housheng, Liu Hong, Tan Wenli, Liu Daiyi, Zeng Yong, and Tang Houpei defrauded Li Deyong of RMB 10 million, apart from paying Li Deyong interest of RMB 1.65 million, the remaining distribution was as follows: Liu Hong received RMB 300,000, Zhong Daoming received RMB 450,000, Zeng Yong received RMB 570,000, Tan Wenli received RMB 520,000, and Tang Housheng received RMB 6.51 million.

Shortly before the maturity date stated on the deposit certificate, Li Deyong contacted Tan Wenli by phone, stating his intention to withdraw the money from Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch. Tan Wenli repeatedly told him to wait a few more days. After Li Deyong repeatedly urged and stated that he would go to the bank himself to withdraw the money, Tan Wenli told Li Deyong that there was no money in the deposit certificate and asked him to speak with Tang Housheng. Tang Housheng told Li Deyong over the phone, "There is no money in the deposit certificate. If you insist on withdrawing, I will only end up in jail, and you won't get the money either. Just wait a few more days." When Li Deyong contacted Tang Housheng again, Tang Housheng kept saying that he would be able to get the money in a few days. Li Deyong had no choice but to agree to a one-month extension by Tang Housheng. On April 15, 2009, Tang Housheng transferred RMB 100,000 to Li Deyong's bank card as interest for the extension.

Li Deyong never went to the Xingjiawan Office of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch with the RMB 10 million deposit certificate and the "Letter of Commitment" to demand payment. On September 3, 2009, Li Deyong reported to the Yunyang County Public Security Bureau of Chongqing that Tang Housheng, Tan Wenli, and others had conspired to defraud him of RMB 10 million. During the investigation by the Yunyang County Public Security Bureau of Chongqing, the Chongqing Municipal Public Security Bureau's Forensic Evidence Identification Center determined that the impression of the "China Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch" seal affixed to the "Letter of Commitment" dated January 15, 2009, held by Li Deyong, differed from the sample seal of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch. On September 22, 2009, the Yunyang County Public Security Bureau of Chongqing served the Chongqing Municipal Public Security Bureau's Forensic Evidence Identification Center's Appraisal Report Yu Gong Jian (Wen) (2009) No. 1264 to Li Deyong. Li Deyong expressed no objection and did not request a supplementary or new appraisal. During the trial, the agents of both Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch and Li Deyong expressed no objection to the appraisal conclusion.

Tang Housheng, Liu Hong, Tan Wenli, Liu Daiyi, Zeng Yong, and Tang Houpei were found by the Chongqing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court in the criminal judgment (2010) Yu Er Zhong Fa Xing Chu Zi No. 105 to have committed financial fraud by using a counterfeit deposit certificate to defraud Li Deyong of RMB 10 million, and were sentenced to penalties and ordered to make restitution of the criminal proceeds. The Chongqing High People's Court, in the criminal ruling (2011) Yu Gao Fa Xing Zhong Zi No. 127, affirmed the original judgment. The criminal judgment (2010) Yu Er Zhong Fa Xing Chu Zi No. 105 of the Chongqing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court has become legally effective. Li Deyong, based on the above criminal judgment, applied for the enforcement and delivery of a car valued at RMB 553,600 belonging to Tan Wenli, Tang Houpei, Liu Qiang, and Tang Xiaodong (four persons). The Chongqing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court has enforced and delivered the property of the above criminals to Li Deyong.

On December 2, 2009, Li Deyong filed a lawsuit, alleging that on January 15, 2009, he went to the Xingjiawan Business Office, a subordinate of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch, and requested the teller to transfer RMB 10 million from his bank account (number 6228 ××××××××××××1610) into a fixed deposit. The teller transferred RMB 10 million from Li Deyong's bank card account and issued a deposit certificate to Li Deyong. The fixed deposit certificate has now matured, and Li Deyong demanded payment. However, Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch refused to pay, claiming that the deposit certificate had been identified by the public security authorities as counterfeit, and that bank employee Tan Wenli and others were suspected of financial fraud, which the public security authorities had placed on file for investigation. Although the "Letter of Commitment" issued by Tan Wenli, an employee of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch, on behalf of the branch, and the RMB 10 million deposit certificate handed over from the bank counter had been identified by the public security authorities as counterfeit, Li Deyong, relying on Tan Wenli's identity as "President" at the Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch premises, trusted that Tan Wenli was acting on behalf of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch in handling his RMB 10 million fixed deposit. Tan Wenli's actions constituted apparent agency, and the consequences should be borne by Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch. Li Deyong requested the court to order Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch to redeem the matured deposit certificate for RMB 10 million and pay interest at an annual rate of 1.71% from January 15, 2009, until the principal and interest are fully paid. The litigation costs were to be borne by Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch.

Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch argued in its defense: 1. The deposit certificate held by Li Deyong was identified as counterfeit and was not delivered to Li Deyong by a teller of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch. There was no deposit transaction or deposit relationship between Li Deyong and Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch. 2. When Li Deyong processed the transfer and withdrawal, he did not express to the teller any intention to convert it into a fixed deposit. His true purpose was to transfer RMB 10 million from his own account into Ren Qiming's account for actual use by Tang Housheng, in order to obtain a high interest return. Li Deyong had an unlawful purpose and was grossly negligent, or even intentional. Therefore, Tan Wenli's actions did not constitute apparent agency, and Li Deyong's losses should be borne by himself. 3. The teller of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch acted in compliance with operational procedures and banking industry practices when processing the transfer transaction. The teller was not at fault in the transaction process, and Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch should not bear civil liability for Li Deyong's losses. The bank requested that Li Deyong's claims be dismissed.

The court of first instance held that Article 6, Paragraph (1) of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Trial of Deposit Certificate Dispute Cases provides: "Where the investor directly delivers funds to the fund user for use, or delivers funds to the fund user through a financial institution, and the financial institution issues a deposit certificate, entry slip, or statement of account to the investor, or enters into a deposit contract with the investor, and the investor obtains or agrees to obtain a high interest margin from the fund user or from the financial institution, the resulting deposit certificate dispute shall be treated as a loan dispute in the form of a deposit certificate." According to the above provision, a loan dispute in the form of a deposit certificate shall have the following legal characteristics: 1. There exists a deposit legal relationship between the investor and the financial institution; 2. There exists a loan legal relationship between the investor and the fund user; 3. The fund user directly or through the financial institution pays a high interest margin to the investor. Li Deyong was fully aware that the monthly interest rate for bank deposits could not be as high as 5.5%. His subjective purpose was to provide financing to the borrower through a bank deposit, thereby ensuring the safety of his funds while obtaining a high interest margin. This determination is supported by the following reasons: First, Li Deyong was contacted by Zhong Daoming. Zhong Daoming, as the depositor, and Liu Daiyi, as the representative of Shengzhou Company, signed a "Capital Attraction and Deposit Agreement." Zhong Daoming collected a deposit of RMB 30,000 from Liu Daiyi and informed Li Deyong of this fact. Li Deyong should have known that there was a specific fund user. Second, at the counter of the Xingjiawan Office of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch, Tan Wenli instructed teller Cheng Jian to process the transfer procedures. Li Deyong and Tan Wenli respectively signed the withdrawal slip and the deposit slip. After the transfer procedures were completed, Li Deyong and others went to the Zhaiba Office of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch to process the transfer of the RMB 1.65 million interest due to Li Deyong. When Liu Hong, Zeng Yong, and others processed the transfer procedures for their respective shares, Li Deyong was present. Li Deyong should have known that his deposit had been transferred to the bank card held by Tan Wenli. Third, after the maturity date stated on the deposit certificate, Li Deyong agreed to a one-month extension by Tang Housheng and received an additional RMB 100,000 as extension interest. Li Deyong obtained a total of RMB 1.75 million in high interest.

This case already possesses two legal characteristics of a loan dispute in the form of a deposit certificate, namely, the existence of a loan legal relationship between the investor and the fund user, and the investor delivering funds directly to the fund user for use or through a financial institution to the fund user, with the fund user directly or through the financial institution paying a high interest margin to the investor. Although objectively no deposit relationship was formed between Li Deyong and Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch, and what occurred was a transfer procedure, Li Deyong's subjective purpose was to provide financing to the borrower through a bank deposit. His actions were based on full trust in the staff of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch processing the relevant procedures at the bank's workplace. Since Tan Wenli was an employee of Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch, and the bank's teller, Cheng Jian, based on his collegial relationship with Tan Wenli, did not inquire about Li Deyong's business intent, did not have Li Deyong sign the deposit slip indicating the destination of the withdrawn funds, and during the transaction, stored and handed out the envelope containing the counterfeit deposit certificate for Tan Wenli, this caused Li Deyong to believe that he had processed a fixed deposit certificate through the bank and then delivered the deposit to the fund user for use. In fact, the RMB 10 million on Li Deyong's bank card was not processed into a fixed deposit certificate but was transferred to Ren Qiming's bank card provided by Tan Wenli and was divided among Tan Wenli and others. Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch played a certain contributory role. Based on these two conditions, this case should be characterized as a loan dispute in the form of a deposit certificate.

Article 6, Paragraph (2), Subparagraph 3 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Trial of Deposit Certificate Dispute Cases provides: "Where the investor delivers the funds to the financial institution, the financial institution issues a deposit certificate, entry slip, or statement of account to the investor, or enters into a deposit contract with the investor, and the investor then designates the financial institution to transfer the funds to the fund user, the fund user shall first return the principal and statutory interest to the investor. The interest shall be calculated at the bank's deposit interest rate for the corresponding period of the People's Bank of China until the date of payment. Due to the fault of the financial institution in assisting the illegal loan, the financial institution shall bear compensation liability for the portion of the principal that the fund user cannot repay, but not exceeding 40% of the portion of the principal that cannot be repaid." According to the above provision, the high interest of RMB 1.75 million prepaid to Li Deyong shall be deducted from the principal. Adding the car valued at RMB 553,600 already enforced and delivered by the court of first instance, Li Deyong has recovered principal of RMB 2,303,600. The remaining principal and statutory interest shall be borne by the fund user. Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch shall bear compensation liability for 40% of the principal that the fund user cannot repay. The judgment was: 1. Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch shall bear compensation liability for 40% of the principal of Li Deyong's deposit of RMB 10 million that the fund user cannot repay; 2. All other claims of Li Deyong were dismissed.

Li Deyong, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed, requesting: to set aside the judgment of first instance and instead order Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch to redeem the RMB 10 million deposit certificate and pay interest; and that Agricultural Bank Yunyang Branch bear the litigation costs of both first and second instances. Reasons: 1. The finding in the judgment of first instance that Li Deyong should have known that his deposit had a specific fund user was inconsistent with the facts found and was erroneous; 2. Several important factual circumstances found in the judgment of first instance were inconsistent with the facts found in the criminal judgment. First, there was no evidence that Zhong Daoming had collected a deposit of RMB 30,000 and informed Li Deyong. Second, the criminal judgment found that Tan Wenli handed Li Deyong "the deposit certificate inside the envelope," not "the envelope" as found in the judgment of first instance; 3. This case is not a loan dispute in the form of a deposit certificate. Tan Wenli's actions constituted apparent agency, and the bank should redeem the deposit.

Yunyang Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China (hereinafter "ABC Yunyang Sub-branch") filed a defense and appealed, requesting: (1) to overturn the judgment of first instance and dismiss Li Deyong's claims; and (2) to impose the litigation costs of the first and second instances on Li Deyong. The reasons were: (1) The cause of action in the first instance was incorrect; this case should be a general certificate of deposit dispute, not a loan dispute in the form of a certificate of deposit. (2) Even if this case were a loan dispute in the form of a certificate of deposit, after the court of first instance had clarified the matter, Li Deyong insisted on not amending his claims, and therefore the court should have dismissed his claims. (3) Li Deyong's conduct did not satisfy the conditions for establishing apparent authority with "good faith and absence of negligence"; therefore, Tan Wenli's conduct did not constitute apparent authority. (4) No deposit contract relationship was formed between Li Deyong and ABC Yunyang Sub-branch, nor did Li Deyong have any actual deposit with that sub-branch; thus, ABC Yunyang Sub-branch had no obligation to pay Li Deyong the principal and interest on the deposit as claimed.

Li Deyong's defense arguments were the same as his grounds for appeal.

The court of second instance held that, according to Article 6(1) of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on the Trial of Certificate of Deposit Dispute Cases, a loan dispute in the form of a certificate of deposit has the following characteristics: there are three or more parties; the legal relationships involved are primarily a deposit relationship between the investor and the financial institution and a loan relationship between the investor and the fund user; there is a flow of funds from the investor to the fund user, and the financial institution provides assistance in that process; the fund user pays high interest to the investor directly or through the financial institution. In this case, first, Li Deyong did not establish a deposit relationship with ABC Yunyang Sub-branch; second, Tan Wenli's conduct could not be attributed to ABC Yunyang Sub-branch, and his conduct could not prove that the bank assisted in the flow of funds. Cheng Jian's act of delivering an envelope containing a counterfeit certificate of deposit, because he delivered it to Tan Wenli rather than to Li Deyong, and because he had a prior acquaintance with Tan Wenli and a pre-arranged agreement, should be deemed Cheng Jian's personal act, not an act in the course of his employment, and could not prove that the bank assisted in the flow of funds. Furthermore, a key fact for a financial institution to be considered as having provided assistance in a loan in the form of a certificate of deposit is that the bank must have obtained a benefit through interest or an interest margin, but ABC Yunyang Sub-branch did not obtain any benefit from the loan involved. Therefore, this case did not meet the legal characteristics of a loan dispute in the form of a certificate of deposit, and the characterization of the case in the first instance was erroneous. In light of the amendment of civil causes of action by the Supreme People's Court, there is currently no such cause of action as "certificate of deposit dispute"; thus, the cause of action in this case should be classified as a dispute over a savings deposit contract.

The specific reasons for finding that no savings deposit contract relationship was formed between Li Deyong and ABC Yunyang Sub-branch are as follows: 1. Li Deyong did not manifest an intention to make a deposit with the bank. First, when conducting a transaction at the counter, Li Deyong did not clearly manifest an intention to deposit RMB 10 million, and he did not object to Tan Wenli's indication to transfer the funds to another bank card; rather, he performed the corresponding operations. Second, the certificate of deposit he held was forged by the perpetrators of the crime involved in this case, not issued by ABC Yunyang Sub-branch. Third, Li Deyong's statements to the public security authorities confirmed that he knew that no separate letter of undertaking was required for conducting a deposit business at the bank, and the seal affixed to the letter of undertaking issued by Tan Wenli was forged, not the act of ABC Yunyang Sub-branch. The foregoing facts demonstrate that Li Deyong did not manifest an intention to deposit funds with the bank, and ABC Yunyang Sub-branch did not accept Li Deyong's offer to deposit. 2. Tan Wenli's conduct could not be attributed to ABC Yunyang Sub-branch. First, Tan Wenli was not the manager of ABC Yunyang Sub-branch, so his conduct could not represent that sub-branch. Second, because Li Deyong himself was at fault, Tan Wenli's conduct did not constitute apparent authority. Li Deyong's fault consisted of: (a) believing that Tan Wenli was the manager of ABC Yunyang Sub-branch based solely on an introduction by a stranger, failing to exercise due diligence; (b) knowing that a bank deposit business must be handled at the counter, yet believing that the letter of undertaking signed by Tan Wenli had the effect of a deposit, without manifesting an intention to deposit at the counter transaction; and (c) having the subjective intent to illegally operate the deposit to obtain high profits. For apparent authority, the counterparty must be in good faith and without fault, only then can it be considered that the counterparty had reason to believe that the actor had authority, constituting apparent authority under Article 49 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China. Judgment: (1) Reverse the judgment of first instance; (2) Dismiss Li Deyong's claims. The litigation costs of the first instance, RMB 81,800, and the litigation costs of the second instance, RMB 81,800, totaling RMB 163,600, shall be borne by Li Deyong.

Li Deyong, dissatisfied with the judgment of second instance, filed an application for retrial with this Court, requesting that the judgment of second instance be set aside and that ABC Yunyang Sub-branch be ordered to perform the obligation of paying the certificate of deposit. (1) The judgment of second instance erred in finding that Li Deyong did not manifest an intention to deposit with the bank on the ground that he did not verbally state a deposit of RMB 10 million to the teller at the savings counter. All relevant persons involved in this case described the business introduced to Li Deyong as a fixed-term deposit of RMB 10 million at ABC Yunyang Sub-branch. Within the business premises of that sub-branch, Li Deyong clearly stated his intention to deposit RMB 10 million to "Manager" Tan Wenli. During the counter operation, Tan Wenli deliberately positioned himself between Li Deyong and the counter, and Li Deyong believed that Tan Wenli was executing his deposit instructions. Teller Cheng Jian did not verify the authenticity of the transaction with Li Deyong himself, and during the operation, he did not adopt the method of recording both the "transferor" and the "payee" on a single receipt; instead, he issued separate withdrawal slips and deposit slips, depriving Li Deyong, as the owner of the funds, of the right to review the transaction. At the same time, while handling the savings business, the teller delivered an envelope containing a counterfeit certificate of deposit to Tan Wenli, resulting in Li Deyong's funds being obtained by criminals through the bank counter transaction. ABC Yunyang Sub-branch did not in any way remind depositors that a manifestation of intention to deposit must be personally made by the depositor to the teller at the counter to be effective. On the contrary, the bank's customer manager service involved customer managers handling relevant matters on behalf of VIP clients at their direction. The bank's use of its internal documents to increase consumer obligations and reduce or exempt the bank's liability is contrary to the legislative intent of standard form contracts and is erroneous.

(2) The judgment of second instance was erroneous in finding that Tan Wenli's conduct did not constitute apparent authority and could not represent ABC Yunyang Sub-branch. It was within the specific environment of ABC Yunyang Sub-branch's office that Li Deyong believed in Tan Wenli's identity as manager and entrusted his bank card to Tan Wenli to handle the relevant deposit business on his behalf. What Li Deyong relied on was ABC Yunyang Sub-branch as represented by Tan Wenli; Tan Wenli's conduct constituted apparent authority, and the consequences of his conduct should be borne by ABC Yunyang Sub-branch.

(3) The act of depositing Li Deyong's funds into another person's account without Li Deyong's consent constituted a material fault of ABC Yunyang Sub-branch, for which the bank should be held liable. Processing business in accordance with the owner's instructions is a fundamental duty of a bank. The criminal case involved in this matter established that Li Deyong indicated to teller Cheng Jian that he wanted to withdraw RMB 10 million from his bank card, but did not indicate that the funds should be transferred to Ren Qiming's account. After withdrawing the funds, teller Cheng Jian, acting on Tan Wenli's arrangement, deposited the funds into Ren Qiming's account, which constituted a material fault.

ABC Yunyang Sub-branch argued in its defense that when Li Deyong handled the bank card transfer of RMB 10 million, he did not manifest an intention to deposit RMB 10 million with ABC Yunyang Sub-branch, nor did he object when the third party, Tan Wenli, told teller Cheng Jian to transfer the funds to Ren Qiming's card; therefore, the savings contract between Li Deyong and the sub-branch was not established. Li Deyong was subjectively at fault, having failed to exercise due diligence and having the intent to illegally obtain high interest; Tan Wenli's conduct did not constitute apparent authority. ABC Yunyang Sub-branch's handling of the business in accordance with the customer's instructions was not in any way irregular, nor was it at fault; it should not bear any liability. The judgment of second instance was clear in its findings of fact and correct in its application of law. Li Deyong's grounds for retrial were inconsistent with the facts and lacked any legal basis and should be dismissed in accordance with the law.

This Court found upon retrial: At the trial of first instance on November 25, 2010, the presiding judge clarified: "In this case, Li Deyong claims a dispute over a savings deposit contract and requests that ABC Yunyang Sub-branch cash the certificate of deposit for RMB 10 million. We now clarify for Li Deyong: if this Court finds that this case does not constitute a savings deposit contract dispute, do you wish to add the fund user or the criminal perpetrator as a party and hold them liable, and do you still request that ABC Yunyang Sub-branch be held liable?" Li Deyong answered: "I still insist on not adding the fund user or the criminal perpetrator as a party and do not request that they be held liable. I request that ABC Yunyang Sub-branch be held liable. If the Court considers it necessary to add them, it may do so ex officio."

The criminal judgment of the Second Intermediate People's Court of Chongqing, Case No. (2010) Yu Er Zhong Fa Xing Chu Zi No. 105, found that in November 2008, Tang Housheng and Liu Daiyi asked Zeng Yong and Liu Hong to "attract capital" for their Shenzhou Company. In December of that same year, Liu Hong proposed using high interest as bait and counterfeit bank certificates of deposit to defraud others of their funds, and suggested that a bank employee cooperate externally, using the bank counter to hand the counterfeit certificate of deposit to the depositor while secretly transferring the depositor's funds into the private accounts of Tang Housheng and others. Tang Housheng and the others agreed. Tang Housheng and Liu Daiyi then invited Tan Wenli, a bank employee, to participate. Tan Wenli agreed in order to recover a loan owed by Tang Housheng. In January 2009, Liu Hong, through Zhong Daoming, was introduced to the depositor Li Deyong, falsely claiming that a deposit of RMB 10 million with the Yunyang County Agricultural Bank for a fixed term of three months would yield a monthly interest of 5.5%. Li Deyong agreed. After the transfer business was completed, Tan Wenli handed the envelope to Li Deyong, who examined the certificate of deposit and believed it to be genuine. In April of the same year, when Li Deyong's three-month "deposit" matured, Tang Housheng had no funds to repay and requested an extension. Li Deyong, realizing he had been defrauded, was forced to agree. In April of the same year, Tang Housheng made a payment of RMB 100,000 to Li Deyong in the name of interest to buy time.

The criminal judgment of the Second Intermediate People's Court of Chongqing, Case No. (2010) Yu Er Zhong Fa Xing Chu Zi No. 105, recorded Li Deyong's statement that on the afternoon of January 14, 2009, Zhong Daoming told him that if he deposited funds in Yunyang for three months, the monthly interest rate would be 5.5%, and the interest would be paid immediately after the deposit. Li Deyong agreed to deposit RMB 10 million. On the way to Yunyang that afternoon, Zhong Daoming introduced Liu Hong and Zeng Yong to Li Deyong. Tan Wenli testified that after the depositor's card funds were transferred into their own accounts, he had Cheng Jian hand out the envelope so that the depositor would believe the funds had indeed been deposited into the bank. Liu Hong testified that when Li Deyong wanted to cash the certificate of deposit at the bank, Tan Wenli told him to contact Tang Housheng, and it was only after Tang Housheng contacted Li Deyong that Li Deyong learned the certificate of deposit was counterfeit.

The other facts found by this Court upon retrial are substantially the same as those found by the court of second instance.

This Court is of the opinion that the disputed issues in the retrial between the parties are: (1) Whether a savings deposit contract was formed between Li Deyong and ABC Yunyang Sub-branch; and (2) Whether ABC Yunyang Sub-branch should be obligated to pay the RMB 10 million funds to Li Deyong.

(1) On the issue of whether a savings deposit contract was formed between Li Deyong and ABC Yunyang Sub-branch.

Article 13 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The parties shall conclude a contract by means of an offer and acceptance." Article 25 of that Law provides: "A contract is concluded when acceptance becomes effective." In accordance with the above legal provisions, the conclusion of a contract necessarily requires the two stages of offer and acceptance. In this case, determining whether a savings deposit contract was formed between Li Deyong and ABC Yunyang Sub-branch requires the following findings:

1. Whether Li Deyong made an offer, i.e., manifested an intention to deposit RMB 10 million with ABC Yunyang Sub-branch.

The facts found in this case show that when Li Deyong conducted business at the Xingjiawan Sub-branch of ABC Yunyang Sub-branch, he did not indicate to the teller that he wished to deposit RMB 10 million. Li Deyong claimed that he clearly stated his intention to deposit to "Manager" Tan Wenli, and that this should be deemed a manifestation of intention to deposit with ABC Yunyang Sub-branch. Whether Li Deyong's claim can be sustained depends on whether Tan Wenli could represent ABC Yunyang Sub-branch, i.e., whether Tan Wenli constituted apparent authority when discussing the deposit matter with Li Deyong. Article 49 of the Contract Law provides: "If an actor who has no power of agency, exceeds the scope of his power of agency, or whose power of agency has terminated concludes a contract in the principal's name, and the counterparty has reason to believe that the actor has the power of agency, the act of agency is effective." The purpose of this provision is to protect the lawful rights and interests of a third party acting in good faith and to promote the security of market transactions. Interpreting the constituent elements of apparent authority in light of the legislative purpose, it must include that the agent's unauthorized act objectively creates an appearance of authority, and that the counterparty, in good faith and without fault, believed that the actor had the power of agency. Good faith and absence of fault on the part of the counterparty should include two aspects: first, the counterparty believed that the agent's conduct was within the scope of the agency; second, the counterparty was not at fault, i.e., the counterparty had exercised sufficient diligence and still could not deny the actor's authority. In this case, Li Deyong, in the course of discussing the deposit with Tan Wenli, failed to exercise reasonable care in the following respects. First, Li Deyong believed Tan Wenli's identity as manager without verification. Li Deyong was introduced to "Manager" Tan Wenli by strangers such as Liu Hong, whom he had just met. Tan Wenli did not receive Li Deyong at the office of ABC Yunyang Sub-branch but at the office of the Yunjian Avenue Sub-branch of ABC Yunyang Sub-branch. As the "manager," Tan Wenli personally took Li Deyong to the counter to handle the "deposit" business. Li Deyong, due to negligence, did not suspect the irregularity of Tan Wenli's conduct as "manager," thus failing to exercise reasonable care. Second, Li Deyong did not suspect the numerous irregular practices in the deposit process. The "Letter of Undertaking" handed to Li Deyong by Tan Wenli stated that ABC Yunyang Sub-branch promised not to "mortgage, inquire, or prematurely withdraw" the funds during the three-month deposit period. The aforementioned promises all pertained to rights that Li Deyong, as the owner of the deposit, could exercise, and the waiver of rights should be made by the right holder. However, "ABC Yunyang Sub-branch" made these promises. Li Deyong should have noticed the irregularity of the content of the letter of undertaking. As a depositor, Li Deyong should have known that when conducting business at the bank counter, he needed to state the type of business to the teller, yet he did not manifest an intention to deposit during the counter transaction. As a depositor who had previously handled bank deposit business, Li Deyong should have known that a deposit slip must be filled out and that the certificate of deposit should be handed directly to the depositor by the teller. Li Deyong did not fill out a deposit slip, and the certificate of deposit was handed out from the bank counter in an envelope. Li Deyong, due to negligence and credulity, did not verify with the counter staff. Third, Li Deyong had the subjective intent to illegally pursue high interest. Zhong Daoming promised Li Deyong a monthly interest rate of 5.5%, which translates to an annual rate of 66%. Li Deyong did not suspect such a high interest rate, nor did he verify it with ABC Yunyang Sub-branch; subjectively, he was not acting in good faith. Because Li Deyong did not meet the constituent elements of good faith and absence of fault required for apparent authority, Tan Wenli's conduct did not constitute apparent authority. Li Deyong's manifestation of intention to deposit made to Tan Wenli cannot be deemed a manifestation of intention made to ABC Yunyang Sub-branch. Li Deyong's argument that, within the specific environment of ABC Yunyang Sub-branch's office, he was led to believe in Tan Wenli's identity as manager and to be convinced that Tan Wenli represented ABC Yunyang Sub-branch, and that deposit business did not require the depositor to personally go to the counter and state the matter to the teller, lacks a basis and is not accepted by this Court.

2. Whether ABC Yunyang Sub-branch made an acceptance.

ABC Yunyang Sub-branch did not issue a savings certificate of deposit to Li Deyong. Li Deyong claimed that the counterfeit certificate of deposit was handed out from the counter of the sub-branch, and therefore the savings deposit contract was formed. From the perspective of Cheng Jian's performance of his duties, what he handed out from the counter was an envelope containing a counterfeit certificate of deposit. There is no evidence in this case that Cheng Jian conspired with Tan Wenli to commit fraud and intentionally handed out the envelope to make Li Deyong believe that a deposit had actually been made. Cheng Jian handed the envelope to Tan Wenli due to a private agreement between them, and there is no evidence that Cheng Jian knew what item was inside the envelope. Therefore, Cheng Jian's act of handing out the envelope was not an act in the performance of his duties. From the perspective of whether Li Deyong could reasonably believe that Cheng Jian's handing out of the envelope was an act in the performance of his duties, during the handling of Li Deyong's business, Li Deyong did not manifest an intention to deposit to Cheng Jian, nor did Cheng Jian ask Li Deyong to fill out a deposit slip or issue a savings certificate of deposit to Li Deyong. Cheng Jian's act of handing an envelope to Tan Wenli was insufficient to cause Li Deyong to believe that a deposit had been made, and his conduct cannot be deemed an act in the performance of his duties, thereby precluding a finding that a fixed-term savings contract for RMB 10 million was formed between ABC Yunyang Sub-branch and Li Deyong.

(2) On the issue of whether ABC Yunyang Sub-branch should be obligated to pay the RMB 10 million funds to Li Deyong.

Article 5 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on the Trial of Certificate of Deposit Dispute Cases provides: "Determination and handling of general certificate of deposit dispute cases. (1) Cases where a party files a lawsuit relying primarily on evidence such as a certificate of deposit, deposit slip, statement of account, or deposit contract, and cases where a financial institution files a lawsuit seeking confirmation that a certificate of deposit, deposit slip, statement of account, or deposit contract is invalid, are general certificate of deposit dispute cases. (2) In trying a general certificate of deposit dispute case, the people's court shall, in addition to examining the authenticity of the certificate of deposit, deposit slip, statement of account, deposit contract, or other such instruments, also examine the authenticity of the deposit relationship between the holder and the financial institution, and shall make a correct determination based on the authenticity of the certificate of deposit, deposit slip, statement of account, deposit contract, or other such instruments and the authenticity of the deposit relationship. (4) In the trial of a certificate of deposit dispute case, if there is sufficient evidence to prove that the certificate of deposit, deposit slip, statement of account, deposit contract, or other such instruments are forged or altered, the people's court shall, on the basis of finding the facts of the case, confirm in accordance with the law that the aforesaid instruments are invalid, and may dismiss the claims of the plaintiff who filed the lawsuit based on the aforesaid instruments or render a judgment based on the actual amount of the deposit." Li Deyong filed the lawsuit based on a certificate of deposit, and this case should be handled as a general certificate of deposit dispute. The certificate of deposit held by Li Deyong was forged, and the RMB 10 million funds covered by that certificate of deposit were not deposited with ABC Yunyang Sub-branch. No savings deposit contract was formed between the parties. Li Deyong's claim, based on a certificate of deposit forged by criminals, that ABC Yunyang Sub-branch should pay the deposit amount stated on the certificate of deposit lacks a legal basis and is not supported by this Court.

Li Deyong argued that Tan Wenli committed the crime using the business premises of ABC Yunyang Sub-branch, causing Li Deyong to believe in Tan Wenli's identity as "manager," and that teller Cheng Jian was at fault in the performance of his duties, resulting in Li Deyong's funds being obtained by criminals through the bank counter. Li Deyong contended that ABC Yunyang Sub-branch was materially at fault for the conduct of its above-mentioned employees and should be held liable. However, given that the court of first instance clarified to Li Deyong that a savings contract relationship might not exist between him and ABC Yunyang Sub-branch, and Li Deyong nevertheless insisted on his original claims without raising any other claims, this Court also deems it inappropriate in the retrial proceedings to hear and adjudicate matters beyond the scope of Li Deyong's claims in the original trial. Any other disputes arising between Li Deyong and ABC Yunyang Sub-branch as a result of the loss of the RMB 10 million funds should be resolved through other legal avenues.

In summary, the judgment of second instance rendered by the Chongqing High People's Court was clear in its findings of fact and correct in its application of law. Pursuant to Article 207, Paragraph 1, and Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

The civil judgment of the Chongqing High People's Court (2012) Yu Gao Fa Min Zhong Zi No. 00014 is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
